value.title: Phase 1 — Claude prep hardened to product
value.summary: Six tasks mirroring guide v1 units tk-0001…tk-0006: PM baseline, four parallel coder lanes, PM composition and real-workload proof.

sections.name: summary
sections.value: Context brief. Purpose: turn the POC Claude prep into product code behind sealed core::prep v2 ports (assets/impl-guide.dd.md architecture.contracts). Entrypoints: `unisphere prep` (crates/app/src/main.rs → crates/app/src/prep.rs), unisphere_sdk::prep::{Preparer, fold_source}, ClaudePrepFold, FileSessionLoader as PrepLoader, ParquetPrepStore. Dependencies: tk-0001 seals before any dispatch; tk-0002…tk-0005 run in parallel clones and import no sibling implementation; tk-0006 imports in order tk-0003, tk-0004, tk-0002, tk-0005. Test approach: pure fold on synthetic fixtures; engine with testkit RecordingFold/MemoryLoader/MemoryPrepStore; store on temp dirs read back through the Parquet Arrow reader; CLI with a fake PrepApi; assembled behaviour through unisphere-proof prep. Hazards: reference-parser window/gap-rounding semantics (re-measure, never round away), state.json growth, same-size same-mtime rewrites, concurrent writers, content leakage into fixtures or evidence. Required proof: vd-0001…vd-0009, vd-000a, vd-000b, vd-0016, vd-0015 per the guide; real-corpus runs only under .harness/temp/prep-real.

tk-0001.assertion: core::prep v2 contract tests pass: every DTO round-trips through serde, status/reason vocabularies and the source-key format are pinned, and a checkpoint with another policy or format is refused.
Arch-check passes with no parquet/arrow/rusqlite/engine edge in core or sdk; output-prep is the only Parquet owner.
`harness checks --json` is ok at the baseline commit with the POC implementations adapted to v2.

tk-0002.assertion: Duplicates of (message.id, requestId) merge by per-field maximum; repeats in a later batch or run emit update sightings; any batch split or checkpoint resume yields identical rows.
cache_creation splits into cw_1h/cw_5m with the fallback main→1h, subagent→5m recorded in cache_write_basis; <synthetic> assistant records become limit_notice events and never calls.
Compaction (trigger, pre/post tokens, duration), recap, scheduled_fire, limit_notice with resets_at_ms where parseable, queue_op and model_switch are typed events; calls carry stop_reason.
Turn origin and sender precedence match extract.py; subagent sources carry parent_session_id; tool_uses pair use and result with outcome, sizes and native duration.
SessionFacts report first/last native event time, the latest main-chain context (sidechains excluded), Some(compaction counts), last_compaction.first_context_after and last_model_switch.
No row carries content unless include_content is set; content_head appears only then; fixtures are synthetic.

tk-0003.assertion: An unchanged re-run reads 0 body bytes and commits nothing; an append reads only bytes after the cursor; rotate, truncate, rewrite and policy change produce Replaced{reason} with a new generation.
An injected commit failure leaves the previous state; the next run recovers without duplicate canonical rows.
Under a concurrent non-LF-aligned writer every run succeeds, pending_tail_bytes is reported and final canonical rows equal a fresh run.

PrepReport counts skipped symlinks, hidden and unreadable entries per set, reports sources excluded by --modified-since as skipped (state kept), uses the full New…Missing vocabulary, reports unsupported harness roots and keys extra roots by label.
record returns exactly the addressed native record only with include_content and is refused before any read otherwise.
fold_source without a store yields the same SessionFacts and checkpoint as run_prep for that source.
The loader opens native files read-only without locks, honours accept, and its anchor detects a same-inode rewrite.

tk-0004.assertion: Commit order is parts → snapshots → state rename; a failure injected before the rename leaves the previous publication readable and the next load removes orphans.
A second writer is refused while the first holds the target lock.
compact rewrites the current generation, drops superseded rows and leaves every canonical view (read back in Rust) unchanged.
Parquet files carry schema-version metadata; views.sql defines every canonical view; the tool_uses table is published.

tk-0005.assertion: The frozen argv (incl. repeated --root HARNESS[:LABEL]=DIR, --harness, --no-default-roots, limits) parse into requests; invalid combinations exit 2.
Machine envelope and human summary render per-set coverage, statuses, skips and pending tails; any Unreadable source exits 3.
`prep record` without --include-content is refused with an actionable next_action.
The prep topic is registered, every example argv in its manifest parses, and README, docs/cli.md and docs/sdk.md carry prep sections.

tk-0006.assertion: unisphere-proof prep: an external SDK consumer with its own store and the built and installed CLI agree across cold, unchanged, append, tail, replace, crash, compact and record scenarios.
The catalogue reports cli_persisted_resume = true for claude-code only.
`harness boot --json` is ready with the prep proof mode included.
Real-corpus parity against a copied extract.py: file-F, four window totals and every call row are exact, or each divergence is explained and accepted by the reviewer.
Live fleet runs and the concurrent-writer copy proof complete with zero failures and final totals equal to a fresh prep.
Claude cold, unchanged and append runs report wall time, peak RSS, bytes read and state.json size against the POC baseline.
An external DuckDB (Python module) reads the published Parquet through views.sql without schema declarations, and view results equal the Rust-read canonical rows.
